{"sectionRef":"§ II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0031","text":"ARTICLE II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES"},{"id":"p0032","text":"Section 2.1 Transfers of Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0033","text":"(a) Transfer and Absolute Assignment of Initial Receivables. In consideration of the Issuer's delivery to the Depositor of the Notes, the Class A Certificate and the Class B Certificate, effective on the Closing Date, the Depositor transfers and absolutely assigns to the Issuer, without recourse (other than the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement), all of the Depositor's right, title and interest, whether now owned or later acquired, in the Initial Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property. The Depositor certifies that the Credit Enhancement Test and the Pool Composition Tests are satisfied for the transfer and assignment of the Initial Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property on the Closing Date."},{"id":"p0034","text":"(b) Transfers and Absolute Assignments of Additional Receivables. Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions in Section 2.1(d), effective on each Acquisition Date, in consideration of the Issuer's distribution to the Depositor of the (i) Additional Receivables Cash"},{"id":"p0035","text":"Transfer Amount for the Additional Receivables to be transferred to the Issuer on that Acquisition Date and (ii) an increase in the Class B Certificate Principal Balance in an amount equal to the excess, if any, of the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount over the Additional Receivables Cash Transfer Amount for such Additional Receivables, the Depositor will transfer and absolutely assign to the Issuer, without recourse (other than the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement), all of the Depositor's right, title and interest, whether then owned or later acquired, in the Additional Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0036","text":"(c) No Assumption of Obligations. These transfers and absolute assignments do not, and are not intended to, include any obligation of the Depositor or any Originator to the Obligors or any other Person relating to the Receivables and the other Depositor Transferred Property, and the Issuer does not assume any of these obligations."},{"id":"p0037","text":"(d) Conditions for Transfers of Additional Receivables. The transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property on each Acquisition Date will be subject to the satisfaction of the following conditions on or before such Acquisition Date:"},{"id":"p0038","text":"(i) Transfer Notice. At least two (2) Business Days before the applicable Acquisition Date, the Administrator shall deliver to the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee a Transfer Notice for the Additional Receivables to be transferred and absolutely assigned on that Acquisition Date, which will specify the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount and attach or include therewith the Schedule of Receivables;"},{"id":"p0039","text":"(ii) Satisfaction of Tests. After giving effect to the transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables by the Depositor to the Issuer, (A) the Credit Enhancement Test is satisfied and (B) the Receivables, in the aggregate, owned by the Issuer, excluding any Temporarily Excluded Receivables, satisfy each of the Pool Composition Tests under Section 3.5(b); and"},{"id":"p0040","text":"(iii) Depositor's Certifications. The Depositor certifies that:"},{"id":"p0041","text":"(A) as of such Acquisition Date, (1) the Depositor is Solvent and will not become insolvent as a result of the transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables on the Acquisition Date, (2) the Depositor does not intend to incur or believe that it would incur debts that would be beyond the Depositor's ability to pay as they matured and (3) the transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables is not made by the Depositor with actual intent to hinder, delay or defraud any Person;"},{"id":"p0042","text":"(B) each of the representations and warranties made by the Depositor under Sections 2.4(a) and 2.4(b), in each case, solely with respect to the related Additional Receivables, will be true and correct as of the Acquisition Date; and"},{"id":"p0043","text":"(C) all conditions to the transfer and assignment of the related Additional Receivables by the Originators to the Depositor under"},{"id":"p0044","text":"2"},{"id":"p0045","text":"Section 2.1(d) of the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement and by the Master Trust to the Depositor under Section 2.1(d) of the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement, as applicable, have been satisfied."},{"id":"p0046","text":"The delivery by the Administrator, on behalf of the Depositor, of the Transfer Notice will be considered a certification by the Depositor that the conditions set forth in this Section 2.1(d) have been satisfied or will be satisfied on the Acquisition Date."},{"id":"p0047","text":"Section 2.2 Acknowledgement of Further Assignments. The Depositor acknowledges that, under the Indenture, the Issuer will assign and pledge the Depositor Transferred Property and related property and rights to the Indenture Trustee for the benefit of the Secured Parties."},{"id":"p0048","text":"Section 2.3 Savings Clause. The Depositor and the Issuer intend that each transfer and assignment under this Agreement be an absolute transfer and assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property, conveying good title to the Depositor Transferred Property free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens, from the Depositor to the Issuer. The Depositor and the Issuer intend that the Depositor Transferred Property not be a part of the Depositor's estate if there is a bankruptcy or insolvency of the Depositor. If, despite the intent of the Depositor and the Issuer, a transfer and assignment of Depositor Transferred Property under this Agreement is determined to be a pledge for a financing or is determined not to be an absolute transfer and assignment, the Depositor Grants to the Issuer a security interest in the Depositor's right, title and interest in the Depositor Transferred Property to secure a loan in an amount equal to all amounts payable by the Depositor under this Agreement, all amounts payable as principal of or interest on the Notes, all amounts payable as Servicing Fees under this Agreement and all other amounts payable by the Issuer under the Transaction Documents. In that case, this Agreement will be a security agreement under Law and the Issuer will have the rights and remedies of a secured party and creditor under the UCC."},{"id":"p0049","text":"Section 2.4 Representations and Warranties About Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0050","text":"(a) Representations and Warranties About Pool of Receivables. The Depositor makes the following representations and warranties about the pool of Receivables on which the Issuer is relying in acquiring the Depositor Transferred Property. The representations and warranties are made as of the Closing Date (for the Initial Receivables) and as of each Acquisition Date (for the related Additional Receivables) and will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement and the pledge of the Depositor Transferred Property by the Issuer to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture."},{"id":"p0051","text":"(i) Valid Transfer and Assignment. This Agreement evidences a valid transfer and absolute assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property from the Depositor to the Issuer, enforceable against creditors of, purchasers from and transferees and absolute assignees of the Depositor."},{"id":"p0052","text":"(ii) Good Title to Depositor Transferred Property. Immediately before the transfer and absolute assignment under this Agreement, the Depositor has good title to"},{"id":"p0053","text":"3"},{"id":"p0054","text":"the Depositor Transferred Property free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens, and, immediately after the transfer and absolute assignment under this Agreement, the Issuer will have good title to the Depositor Transferred Property, free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens."},{"id":"p0055","text":"(iii) Security Interest in Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0056","text":"(A) This Agreement creates a valid and continuing security interest (as defined in the applicable UCC) in the Depositor Transferred Property in favor of the Issuer, which is prior to any Lien, other than Permitted Liens, and is enforceable against all creditors of, purchasers from and transferees and absolute assignees of the Depositor."},{"id":"p0057","text":"(B) All filings (including UCC filings) necessary in any jurisdiction to give the Depositor a first priority, validly perfected ownership and security interest in the Originator Transferred Property and the Master Trust Transferred Property, to give the Issuer a first priority, validly perfected ownership and security interest in the Depositor Transferred Property and to give the Indenture Trustee a first priority perfected security interest in the Collateral, will be made within ten (10) days after the Closing Date or the related Acquisition Date, as applicable."},{"id":"p0058","text":"(C) All financing statements filed or to be filed against the Depositor in favor of the Issuer describing the Depositor Transferred Property transferred under this Agreement will contain a statement to the following effect: \"A purchase, absolute assignment or transfer of or security interest in any collateral described in this financing statement will violate the rights of the Secured Party/Assignee.\""},{"id":"p0059","text":"(D) The Depositor has not authorized the filing of and is not aware of any financing statements against the Depositor that include a description of collateral covering any Depositor Transferred Property other than the financing statements relating to the security interest Granted to the Depositor under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement or by the Issuer to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture, or that has been terminated."},{"id":"p0060","text":"(b) Representations and Warranties About Security Interest. If the transfer and absolute assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property under this Agreement is determined to be a pledge relating to a financing or is determined not to be a transfer and absolute assignment, the Depositor makes the following representations and warranties on which the Issuer is relying in acquiring the Depositor Transferred Property, which representations and warranties are made as of the Closing Date or as of the related Acquisition Date, as applicable,"},{"id":"p0061","text":"4"},{"id":"p0062","text":"will survive termination of this Agreement and may not be waived by the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee:"},{"id":"p0063","text":"(i) Valid Security Interest. This Agreement creates a valid and continuing security interest (as defined in the applicable UCC) in the Depositor Transferred Property in favor of the Issuer, which is prior to all other Liens, other than Permitted Liens, and is enforceable against creditors of, purchasers from and transferees and absolute assignees of the Depositor."},{"id":"p0064","text":"(ii) Type. Each Receivable is (A) if the Receivable is not secured by the related Device, an \"account\" or \"payment intangible,\" or (B) if the Receivable is secured by the related Device, \"chattel paper,\" in each case, within the meaning of the applicable UCC."},{"id":"p0065","text":"(iii) Good Title. Immediately before the transfer and absolute assignment under this Agreement, the Depositor owns and has good title to the Depositor Transferred Property free and clear of all Liens, other than Permitted Liens. The Depositor has received all consents and approvals required by the terms of the Depositor Transferred Property to Grant to the Issuer its right, title and interest in the Depositor Transferred Property, except to the extent the requirement for consent or approval is extinguished under the applicable UCC."},{"id":"p0066","text":"(iv) Filing Financing Statements. The Depositor has caused, or will cause within ten (10) days after the Closing Date, the filing of all appropriate financing statements in the proper filing office in the appropriate jurisdictions under applicable Law to perfect the security interest Granted in the Depositor Transferred Property to the Issuer under this Agreement. All financing statements filed or to be filed against the Depositor in favor of the Issuer under this Agreement describing the Depositor Transferred Property will contain a statement to the following effect: \"A purchase, absolute assignment or transfer of or grant of a security interest in any collateral described in this financing statement will violate the rights of the Secured Parties.\""},{"id":"p0067","text":"(v) No Other Transfer, Grant or Financing Statement. Other than the security interest Granted to the Issuer under this Agreement, the Depositor has not transferred or Granted a security interest in any of the Depositor Transferred Property. The Depositor has not authorized the filing of and is not aware of any financing statements against the Depositor that include a description of collateral covering any of the Depositor Transferred Property, other than financing statements relating to the security interest Granted to the Issuer. The Depositor is not aware of any judgment or tax Lien filings against it."},{"id":"p0068","text":"Section 2.5 Originators' Reacquisition and Servicer's Acquisition of Receivables for Breach of Representations."},{"id":"p0069","text":"(a) Representations and Warranties from Receivables Transfer Agreements. Each Originator and the Servicer, severally has made, as of the Closing Date, and each Originator or the Servicer, as applicable, severally will make, as of each Acquisition Date, the Eligibility"},{"id":"p0070","text":"5"},{"id":"p0071","text":"Representation about the Receivables transferred and absolutely assigned by such Originator or the Master Trust, respectively, on that date, and has consented to the transfer by the Depositor to the Issuer of the Depositor's rights to such Eligibility Representation. The Issuer is relying on each applicable Originator's or the Servicer's Eligibility Representation in acquiring the Receivables, which Eligibility Representation will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Receivables by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement and the pledge of the Receivables to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture."},{"id":"p0072","text":"(b) Reacquisition or Acquisition. Under Section 2.1(a), the Depositor has transferred and absolutely assigned to the Issuer the Depositor's rights under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, including the right to require (i) an Originator to reacquire any Receivables transferred and absolutely assigned by it under the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement or (ii) the Servicer to acquire any Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by the Master Trust under the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement, in each case, for which such party has made the Eligibility Representation if, in each case, there is a breach of such Eligibility Representation, such breach is not cured and such breach results in a material adverse effect on the Issuer. If any Originator or the Servicer breaches the Eligibility Representation made by it with respect to any Receivable transferred by such Originator or the Master Trust, respectively, to the Depositor, such breach is not cured and such breach has a material adverse effect on the Issuer, then the Depositor will enforce such Originator's or the Servicer's obligation, as applicable, to reacquire or acquire, respectively, any such Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by it to the Depositor for which the Eligibility Representation was breached pursuant to Section 3.4 of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."},{"id":"p0073","text":"(c) Reacquisition or Acquisition Sole Remedy. The sole remedy of the Depositor, the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee for a breach of any Eligibility Representation is to require the related Originator or the Servicer, as applicable, to reacquire or acquire, respectively, the Receivable under Section 3.4 of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."},{"id":"p0074","text":"Section 2.6 Originators' Reacquisition or Servicer's Acquisition of Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivables."},{"id":"p0075","text":"(a) Reacquisition or Acquisition. Under Section 2.1(a), the Depositor has transferred and absolutely assigned to the Issuer the Depositor's rights under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, including the right to require (i) an Originator to reacquire any Receivables transferred and absolutely assigned by it under the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement or (ii) the Servicer to acquire any Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by the Master Trust under the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement, in each case, when such Receivable becomes a Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable. If any Receivable becomes a Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable, the Depositor will enforce such Originator's or the Servicer's obligation, as applicable, to reacquire or acquire, respectively, any such Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by it to the Depositor pursuant to Section 4.6 or 4.7, respectively, of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."},{"id":"p0076","text":"(b) Reacquisition or Acquisition Sole Remedy. If a Receivable becomes a Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable, the sole remedy of the Depositor, the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee is to require the related Originator or the Servicer, as applicable, to reacquire"},{"id":"p0077","text":"6"},{"id":"p0078","text":"or acquire, respectively, the Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable under Section 4.6 or 4.7, respectively, of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."}]}

content.content: [{"id":"p0108","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"Section 3.3 Servicer's Acquisition of Receivables."},{"id":"p0109","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(a) Acquisition for Servicer Modifications. If extensions, modifications, amendments, cancellations or waivers of Receivables or any terms thereof are made that would require such Receivables to be acquired under Section 3.2(b), the Servicer will acquire all such Receivables as set forth in Section 3.3(d)."},{"id":"p0110","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(b) Acquisition for Breach of Servicer's Obligations. If a Responsible Person of the Servicer receives written notice from the Depositor, the Issuer, the Owner Trustee or the"},{"id":"p0111","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"9"},{"id":"p0112","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"Indenture Trustee of a breach of the Servicer's obligations in Section 3.2(c) or (d), and the Servicer fails to correct such failure or impairment in all material respects by the end of the second month following the month in which the Servicer received such written notice, the Servicer will acquire all Receivables with respect to which such breach was not so cured as set forth in Section 3.3(d)."},{"id":"p0113","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(c) Acquisition for System Limitation or Inability to Service. If the Servicer, in its sole discretion, determines that as a result of a receivables systems error or receivables systems limitation or for any other reason the Servicer is unable to service a Receivable according to the Servicing Procedures and the terms of this Agreement, the Servicer may acquire the relevant Receivable as set forth in Section 3.3(d)."},{"id":"p0114","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(d) Acquisition of Receivables; Payment of Acquisition Amount. For any acquisition of a Receivable by the Servicer under this Section 3.3, the Servicer will acquire the Receivable by remitting the related Acquisition Amount on or prior to the second Business Day before the Payment Date related to the Collection Period in which such Receivable was acquired by the Servicer. If Cellco is the Servicer, it may pay any Acquisition Amounts according to Section 4.3(c)."},{"id":"p0115","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(e) Transfer and Assignment of Acquired Receivables. When the Servicer's payment of the Acquisition Amount for a Receivable is included in Available Funds for a Payment Date, the Issuer will be deemed to have transferred and assigned to the Servicer, effective as of the last day of the Collection Period immediately preceding the related Collection Period, all of the Issuer's right, title and interest in the Receivable and all security and documents relating to the Receivable. The transfer and assignment will not require any action by the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee and will be without recourse, representation or warranty by the Issuer except the representation that the Issuer owns the Receivable free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens. After the transfer and assignment, the Servicer will mark its receivables systems to indicate that the receivable is no longer a Receivable and may take any action necessary or advisable to transfer the Receivable free from any Lien of the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee."},{"id":"p0116","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(f) No Obligation to Investigate. None of the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Successor Servicer hereunder), the Sponsor, the Marketing Agent, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator or the Servicer will be obligated to investigate whether a breach or other event has occurred that would require the acquisition of any Receivable under this Section 3.3 or whether any Receivables are otherwise required to be acquired under this Section 3.3."},{"id":"p0117","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(g) Acquisition is Sole Remedy. The sole remedy of the Issuer, the Indenture Trustee, the Owner Trustee, and the Secured Parties for any extension, modification, amendment, cancellation or waiver of a Receivable or any terms thereof under Section 3.2(b) or a breach of the covenants made by the Servicer in Section 3.2(c) or (d) is the Servicer's acquisition of the Receivables, as described under this Section 3.3."}]

[{"id":"p0282","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"Section 6.2 Liability of Servicer and Marketing Agent."},{"id":"p0283","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(a) Liability for Specific Obligations. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable under this Agreement only for its specific obligations under this Agreement. All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement."},{"id":"p0284","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(b) No Liability of Others. Each of the Servicer's and the Marketing Agent's obligations under this Agreement are corporate obligations. No Person will have recourse, directly or indirectly, to any member, manager, officer, director, employee or agent of the Servicer for the Servicer's obligations or the Marketing Agent for the Marketing Agent's obligations, as applicable, under this Agreement."},{"id":"p0285","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(c) Legal Proceedings. The Servicer will not be required to start, pursue or participate in any legal proceeding that is not incidental or related to its obligations to service the Receivables under this Agreement and that in its opinion may result in liability or cause it to pay or risk funds or incur financial liability. The Servicer may in its sole discretion start or pursue any legal proceeding to protect the interests of the Noteholders or the Depositor under the Transaction Documents. The Servicer will be responsible for the fees and expenses of legal counsel and any liability resulting from the legal proceeding."},{"id":"p0286","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(d) Force Majeure. Neither the Servicer nor the Marketing Agent will be responsible or liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement caused by, directly or indirectly, forces beyond its control, including strikes, work stoppages, acts of war, terrorism, civil or military disturbances, fire, flood, earthquakes, storms, hurricanes or other natural disasters or failures of mechanical, electronic or communication systems; provided, however that this provision shall not limit the right to remove the Servicer for a Servicer Termination Event as provided in Section 7.2(a), other than with respect to the extension of the grace periods as provided in Section 7.2(a). Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, as applicable, will use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance as soon as practicable in the circumstances."},{"id":"p0287","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(e) Reliance by Servicer and Marketing Agent. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent may rely in good faith on the advice of counsel or on any document believed to be genuine and to have been executed by the proper party for any matters under this Agreement."},{"id":"p0288","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"Section 6.3 Indemnities of Servicer and the Marketing Agent."},{"id":"p0289","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"29"},{"id":"p0290","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(a) Indemnification."}]

The Servicer may grant extensions, refunds, rebates or adjustments on any Receivable or amend any Receivable according to the Servicing Procedures."},{"id":"p0099","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"However, if the Servicer (i) grants payment extensions resulting in the final payment date of the Receivable being later than the Collection Period immediately preceding the Final Maturity Date for the latest maturing Class of Notes, (ii) cancels a Receivable or reduces or waives (including with respect to any Upgrade Offer) the remaining Principal Balance under a Receivable or any portion thereof and/or as a result, the monthly payments due thereunder, or (iii) modifies, supplements, amends or revises a Receivable to grant the Obligor under such Receivable a contractual right to upgrade the related Device, it will acquire the affected Receivable solely as described under Section 3.3, unless it is required to take the action by Law."},{"id":"p0100","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"In addition, if the Marketing Agent or the Servicer (x) applies a payment or grants a credit to an Obligor with respect to cancellations, prepayments or invoicing errors the Servicer may apply such credits either directly to the applicable device payment plan agreement or in accordance with its customary payment application procedures set forth above and (y) applies a payment or grants a credit to an Obligor under a Receivable in connection with an Upgrade Offer as set forth in Section 3.12(b), the Servicer will apply such credits directly to the applicable device payment plan agreement and will not apply such credits in accordance with its customary payment application procedures set forth above."},{"id":"p0101","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"8"},{"id":"p0102","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(c) Maintenance of Security Interests in the Receivables. The Servicer will maintain perfection of the security interest of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee in each Receivable."},{"id":"p0103","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(d) No Impairment. The Servicer will not impair in any material respect the rights of the Issuer or the Noteholders in any Receivable except as permitted by this Agreement."},{"id":"p0104","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(e) Assignment for Enforcement. Effective as of the related Cutoff Date, the Receivables are assigned to the Servicer solely for the purpose of permitting the Servicer to perform its servicing and administrative obligations under this Agreement, including the start or pursuit of or participation in a legal proceeding to enforce its rights or remedies with respect to a Receivable or such other Proceeding otherwise related to a Receivable. If in a legal proceeding it is held that the Servicer may not enforce its rights or remedies with respect to a Receivable on the grounds that it is not a real party in interest or a holder entitled to enforce rights or remedies with respect to the Receivable, the Issuer will, at the Servicer's expense and direction, assign the Receivable to the Servicer solely for that purpose or take steps to enforce its rights and remedies with respect to the Receivable, including bringing suit in the names of the Indenture Trustee, the Noteholders and the Issuer."},{"id":"p0105","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(f) Powers of Attorney. The Issuer appoints the Servicer as the Issuer's attorney-in-fact, with full power of substitution to exercise all rights of the Issuer for the servicing and administration of the Receivables. This power of attorney, and all authority given, under this Section 3.2(f) is revocable and is given solely to facilitate the performance of the Servicer's obligations under this Agreement and may only be used by the Servicer consistent with this Agreement. On request of the Servicer, the Issuer will furnish the Servicer with written powers of attorney and other documents to enable the Servicer to perform its obligations under this Agreement."},{"id":"p0106","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(g) Release Documents. The Servicer is authorized to execute and deliver, on behalf of itself, the Issuer, the Indenture Trustee and the Noteholders any documents of satisfaction, cancellation, partial or full release or discharge, and other comparable documents, for the Receivables."},{"id":"p0107","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","text":"(h) Enforcement of Receivables Under an Upgrade Offer. If an Obligor accepts an Upgrade Offer with respect to a Receivable but fails to satisfy the required terms and conditions related to such Upgrade Offer, the Servicer agrees to (i) not waive any amounts due by such Obligor under the related Receivable and pursue its Servicing Procedures against such Obligor in respect of the related Receivable until all amounts due under the related Receivable are received and (ii) enforce, on behalf of the Issuer, any rights and obligations under the related Receivable."}]

input.quote: The Issuer is relying on each applicable Originator's or the Servicer's Eligibility Representation in acquiring the Receivables, which Eligibility Representation will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Receivables by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement and the pledge of the Receivables to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture.
input.rationale: Translated to this receivables-transfer/servicing structure, the warranty package exceeds the preferred position and no redline is warranted. (1) Performance standard: Section 3.2(a) (p0082) requires the Servicer to "manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures" — the industry-standard/workmanlike-manner analogue. (2) Conformance warranty: the Originators' and Servicer's Eligibility Representation about each Receivable (Section 2.5(a), p0071) is not period-limited at all; it expressly survives the transfer and the Indenture pledge (and the Section 2.4(b) security-interest reps survive termination and may not be waived), which is materially longer than the preferred 12 months. (3) Real remedy: Sections 2.5(b)/(c) and 2.6 give a mandatory reacquisition/acquisition obligation at the Acquisition Amount for uncured breaches with a material adverse effect — economically the "refund" limb of repair/replace/refund — backed by Section 3.3 acquisition obligations for the Servicer's own breaches and, importantly, the Section 11.2 dispute-resolution backstop (p0450) allowing the Issuer, Indenture Trustee or Noteholders to compel mediation or binding arbitration if a repurchase request is unresolved after 180 days. (4) Compliance with laws is separately warranted at Section 6.1(a)(ix) (p0268) plus Servicing Procedures compliance at 6.1(a)(x). No "AS IS" language or implied-warranty disclaimer exists anywhere in the agreement, so nothing swallows the express representations. Noted but not flagged: the "sole remedy" framing in Sections 2.5(c)/2.6(b)/3.3(g) and the willful-misconduct/bad-faith/gross-negligence liability standard in Section 6.2(a) narrow recourse, but these are standard ABS constructs and the mandatory repurchase remains a specific, enforceable obligation; the malicious-code limb of the preferred position has no application to a receivables pool.

system.text:
You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-d2bcb466","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"Section 6.3 contains a counterparty-side indemnity running in our favour: Cellco as Servicer (and separately as Marketing Agent) indemnifies the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee and their personnel for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees) resulting from its willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, including costs of enforcing the indemnity. Section 6.3(b) supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition unless prejudicial, Servicer/Marketing Agent may assume defence with counsel reasonably satisfactory to us, separate counsel at its cost on conflict, no settlement implying our acknowledgement without consent), and Section 6.3(c) provides survival past resignation, termination and trust termination. The indemnity is uncapped (no super-cap or fee-based ceiling) and there is no reciprocal Issuer/Depositor indemnity of the Servicer anywhere in the Agreement, so we sit at or above the preferred position on the material terms (Vendor indemnity for gross negligence/wilful misconduct plus standard procedure, with our own indemnity narrower than "narrow"). Section 7.5(c) additionally puts servicing-transition expenses on the resigning or terminated Servicer. Sub-elements short of preferred, noted only: there is no IP-infringement indemnity (atypical and commercially inapposite for a receivables securitisation with no services/deliverables licensed to us), no express standalone trigger for breach of applicable law or unauthorised disclosure of data (though Section 6.2(a) preserves liability for the Servicer's own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, and Exhibit A privacy/data protection policies apply), and the Depositor is not itself named as an Indemnified Person. These are not material failures of the fallback, so no redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-274f8f50","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES","rationale":"Direction of ownership runs in our favour throughout. Section 2.1(a)/(b) has the Depositor "transfer and absolutely assign to the Issuer... all of the Depositor's right, title and interest" in the Receivables and related Depositor Transferred Property; Section 9.2 bars any further transfer or Lien; Section 9.4(a) requires Cellco to flag its own receivables systems to show the Receivables are owned by the Issuer; and Section 3.10(b) has the Custodian hold the Receivable Files "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee", with Section 7.5(b) requiring delivery of the Receivable Files and the accounts and records to a Successor Servicer. Nothing assigns our property, records or obligor data to Cellco, and no joint ownership is created, so there is no walk-away exposure. This is a securitisation transfer and servicing agreement rather than a procurement contract, so there is no classic deliverables/work-product IP clause; the only counterparty-favourable carve-out is Section 7.5(b), under which the Servicer "will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications" — that is Cellco retaining its own platform, tools and know-how, which the playbook expressly permits and which sits at the fallback position (vendor keeps generic tools; we keep the files, records and data we own). We note in passing the absence of an express licence-back of servicing software or systems to support a servicing transition, which is a sub-element short of the preferred position but not a material failure warranting a redline here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-74ba522d","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"The liability architecture here is mutual and, on its material terms, sits at or above the fallback, so no redline is warranted.

1. Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (p0283) limits the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's liability to their specific obligations and to their own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence. Section 5.2(a) (p0243) applies word-for-word the same limitation to the Depositor. The limitation is therefore symmetrical and not a one-sided vendor shield — the walk-away scenario (our liability uncapped while the counterparty's is capped) does not arise.

2. No monetary cap on the counterparty: there is no dollar or months-of-fees cap anywhere in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" or consequential-damages exclusion language; the only damages limitation found is the arbitral panel's limited remedial power at p0469). For us this is better than the preferred 12-months'-fees / USD 1,000,000 formulation. Importing a fees-based cap would be actively adverse: the Servicing Fee in this structure is a small monthly percentage of principal balance, so a 12-month-fees cap would be illusory and would materially reduce Cellco's exposure. Consistent with the rule's own warning about caps measured against a small fee base, we should not propose one.

3. Carve-outs: the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's indemnities under Section 6.3(a) (p0291, p0292) run to the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, damages and liabilities resulting from willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, with no cap and no super-cap ceiling. Indemnification, gross negligence and willful misconduct — the fallback's minimum carve-out set — are all outside any limitation, and "bad faith" substantially covers the fraud carve-out.

4. Our side is additionally protected: Section 9.6 (p0378) limits any claim against the Depositor or the Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property, an effective ceiling on our exposure that the counterparty does not enjoy.

Noted but not flagged (minor sub-elements per the classification rules): there is no express uncapped carve-out for confidentiality, data protection/security or infringement of our IP, no separate fraud carve-out beyond "bad faith", and no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion. Given that the counterparty carries no monetary cap at all and its indemnities are uncapped, these omissions do not defeat the fallback and are recorded for information rather than redlined. This is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement rather than a commercial supply contract, and the exculpation-plus-uncapped-indemnity model is the market-standard equivalent of the playbook position.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-aa0b073e","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"The assignment architecture is symmetric and preserves our successor rights, so it sits at or above the fallback. Section 10.2(a) is expressly subject to Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6: Section 5.3 lets our Depositor pass this Agreement to any Person into which it merges or consolidates, that succeeds to its business, or that is an Affiliate to whom it assigns, without counterparty consent — the affiliate/successor and M&A carve-out the preferred position requires (the 15-Business-Day assumption agreement, Officer's Certificate/Opinion and Rating Agency notice are mechanical successor formalities, close to the fallback's "written notice"). Section 7.6 gives Cellco as Servicer the mirror-image right, and the residual consent gate in 10.2(a) runs to the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and Noteholders (investor protection) rather than to Cellco, so the counterparty holds no veto over our assignments. The Issuer's ability to assign and pledge to the Indenture Trustee is expressly acknowledged (Section 2.2), and Section 10.2(b) binds permitted successors and assigns. On change of control: the phrase appears nowhere in the Agreement, and there is no Cellco right to terminate, re-price or refuse consent on a change of control of the Issuer or Depositor — to the contrary, Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer unless it is legally unable to perform. The Class A Certificateholder's Optional Acquisition/Optional Redemption rights (Sections 8.1–8.2) are principal-balance and date triggered, not change-of-control triggered, so they are not a walk-away exit right. Noted but not flagged: consent under 10.2(a) is not qualified by a "not unreasonably withheld" standard and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor, both minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording in a structured-finance deal where the consent parties are the trustees and noteholders.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-7c3430fb","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The agreement imposes no exclusivity, "sole supplier" or requirements-purchase obligation on our side (Issuer/Depositor), which meets the preferred position. Searches for "exclusive"/"sole" return only the Cap Collateral Account control provisions (Sections in Article IX), non-exclusive jurisdiction in Section 10.6, and "sole remedy"/"sole discretion" usages — none of which restrict our freedom to engage other providers. The Section 3.1 engagement of Cellco as Servicer (and the Section 3.10/3.11 custodian and marketing agent appointments) is a structural single-servicer appointment rather than an exclusive dealing covenant, and it is not stated to be exclusive; Article VII expressly permits Servicer resignation/termination on Servicer Termination Events and the engagement of a Successor Servicer (including an unaffiliated institution servicing consumer receivables), so there is no term-length lock-in and no performance-exit gap. Nothing to redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-b0980a4b","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/termination fee payable by us (the Issuer or Depositor) to Cellco: full-text searches for "liquidated damages" and "penalty" return nothing, and the only amounts we owe the counterparty are ordinary compensation for services actually rendered (Servicing Fee at 0.75%, Supplemental Servicing Fee, Temporarily Excluded Receivables Servicing Fee under p0134). This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages. We reviewed the planner's candidates: (i) the $150,000 appointment fee and the Additional Successor Servicer Fee (excess of $425,000 over the Servicing Fee, p0570) are compensation to a third-party Successor Servicer for work performed after Cellco resigns or is removed, not a penalty running to the counterparty, and the correlative transition expenses are pushed onto the resigning or terminated Servicer under Section 7.5(c), a term that benefits us; and (ii) the Make-Whole Payment is yield maintenance payable to Noteholders on an Issuer-elected Optional Redemption (p0358), not a breach-triggered charge payable to the counterparty, and it is expressly excluded on a Clean-Up Redemption (p0351). Both fall outside this rule's direction test, so no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-2438dd24","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"Section 7.5(b) is the only provision in the Agreement that addresses licensing of the Servicer's systems, and it lands squarely in walk-away territory: the Servicer is expressly not obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to any Successor Servicer or third party, so there is no licence at all to the Issuer, its Affiliates or the contractors/Successor Servicer who would need to run the servicing platform, and no path to add them. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Issuer / Depositor)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. On the whole, the document is materially favourable to us: the counterparty-side (Cellco, as Servicer / Marketing Agent) indemnity in Section 6.3 is uncapped and unreciprocated, the liability limitation in Section 6.2(a) is mirrored word-for-word against the Depositor in Section 5.2(a) with no monetary cap on the counterparty, ownership of the Receivables, Receivable Files and records runs to the Issuer, assignment rights are symmetric with successor and Affiliate carve-outs, and governing law and venue are New York. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment, auto-renewal, customer-payable liquidated damages or audit exposure binding our side. Section 7.5 transition assistance and Section 7.3 continued performance are better than our preferred position, and Section 7.5(c) puts transition expenses on the outgoing Servicer.

Three items require action and one requires manual completion:

- **Licence grant (high, deviation).** Section 7.5(b) expressly relieves the Servicer of any obligation to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to a Successor Servicer or third party. There is no licence at all in our favour, which fails both our preferred and fallback positions and sits in walk-away territory on a servicing transfer.
- **Termination for convenience (medium, deviation).** Our only exit from the servicing engagement requires a Servicer Termination Event under Section 7.2, and the removal right sits with the Indenture Trustee at the Controlling Class's direction rather than with the Issuer or Depositor; Section 8.3 otherwise runs the Agreement to the last Receivable. The Vendor side of this rule is over-satisfied (Section 7.1 bars resignation absent legal inability), so the gap is one-sided against us.
- **Insurance (low, missing).** There is no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement, notwithstanding that the Servicer/Custodian holds and processes Obligor personally identifiable information and may subcontract under Section 6.4. The Section 6.3 indemnity (willful misconduct, bad faith, gross negligence only) is not a substitute.
- **Performance warranty (medium, needs review).** The automated review did not complete for this rule and must be worked manually before we sign off.

We are not proposing a monetary liability cap. The counterparty currently carries none, and a fees-based cap measured against a Servicing Fee of 0.75% of principal balance would be illusory and actively adverse to us.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer (Section 7.5(b)) |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer (Sections 7.1–7.2; § VIII, 8.3) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § X Miscellaneous (no provision through Section 10.13) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review** | Not yet identified — review incomplete |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Sections 6.3(a)–(c)) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § II Transfer and Acquisition of Depositor Transferred Property (Sections 2.1–2.2; 3.10(b); 7.5(b); 9.2; 9.4(a)) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Section 6.2(a); cf. 5.2(a), 6.3(a), 9.6) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Section 10.2; cf. 5.3, 7.4, 7.6) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Section 3.1; cf. Article VII) |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Section 7.5(c)) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Sections 3.6, 3.4(e); Article XIV) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Sections 10.5–10.6; cf. Article XI) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § IV Accounts, Collections and Application of Funds (cf. Section 2.1(d)) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § VIII Termination (Sections 8.1–8.3) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Sections 7.3, 7.5) |

### Notes on the compliant items sitting at the fallback

- **IP.** Section 7.5(b)'s retention by the Servicer of its own processes, models, servicing software and know-how sits at the fallback (vendor keeps generic tools; we keep the files, records and data we own). The absence of a transition licence-back is addressed under LICENSE rather than here.
- **GOVLAW.** The submission to jurisdiction in Section 10.6 is nonexclusive rather than exclusive. This is a minor sub-element and preserves our own flexibility, so we do not redline it.
- **ASSIGN.** Consent under Section 10.2(a) is not qualified by "not unreasonably withheld" and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor. Minor, and the consent parties are the trustees and Noteholders rather than Cellco.
- **TRANSITION.** Delivery under Section 7.5 is "as soon as practicable" rather than on a fixed 30-day clock, with no machine-readable format or deletion certification. Proportionate here given Section 7.3 continued performance and Section 3.12(b)/Exhibit A cooperation and data-protection obligations.
- **INDEMN.** No IP-infringement indemnity and no standalone trigger for breach of law or unauthorised data disclosure, and the Depositor is not a named Indemnified Person. Not material failures given the uncapped Section 6.3 indemnity.
- **LOL-CAP.** No express uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection or IP infringement, no separate fraud carve-out beyond "bad faith", and no mutual consequential-damages exclusion. Recorded for information only; the counterparty carries no cap at all.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Section 7.5(b) — no licence to servicing systems on transition.** The Servicer is expressly not obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to any Successor Servicer or third party. There is no licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates or its contractors, and no mechanism to add them, so a Successor Servicer would have no right to run the platform needed to service the Receivables. This fails both the preferred and fallback positions and is our principal open point.
2. **Absence of any insurance covenant where the counterparty processes personal data.** The Servicer/Custodian holds Obligor personally identifiable information and may contract with other Persons under Section 6.4, with no coverage requirement anywhere in the Agreement. This engages the playbook's walk-away scenario for a vendor processing personal data; the Section 6.3 indemnity does not cure it.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the licence redline (priority).** Recast Section 7.5(b) so that the carve-out becomes a non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates and its contractors (including any Successor Servicer), transferable to successors and limited to what is necessary to service the Receivables, while preserving the Servicer's carve-outs for genuine third-party transfer and confidentiality restrictions and for legal, regulatory, privacy and data-protection limits.
2. **Propose a convenience termination right.** Insert a new Section 7.1A giving the Issuer, at the Depositor's direction, the right to terminate the Servicer on 30 days' notice without fee or penalty and with refund of prepaid Servicing Fees, plugged into the existing Sections 7.3–7.5 transition machinery so Noteholder continuity is preserved. Offer 60–90 days' notice as our fallback.
3. **Add an insurance covenant.** Insert a new Section 10.14 requiring the Servicer/Marketing Agent to maintain CGL (USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate), E&O (USD 2M), cyber (USD 5M) and workers' compensation cover, with certificates on request. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M to be offered in the comment.
4. **Complete the performance warranty review.** The WARRANTY rule review failed to complete and must be run manually against the Agreement before we clear the document.
5. **Hold the line on liability.** Do not table a monetary liability cap. The counterparty is presently uncapped, its Section 6.3 indemnities are uncapped, and Section 9.6 already limits recourse against the Depositor and Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property.
6. **Confirm business sign-off** on the fallback-level items listed in Section 2 above, which we do not propose to redline."}

- **INDEMN.** No IP-infringement indemnity and no standalone trigger for breach of law or unauthorised data disclosure, and the Depositor is not a named Indemnified Person. Not material failures given the uncapped Section 6.3 indemnity.
- **LOL-CAP.** No express uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection or IP infringement, no separate fraud carve-out beyond "bad faith", and no mutual consequential-damages exclusion. Recorded for information only; the counterparty carries no cap at all.

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Section 7.5(b) — no licence to servicing systems on transition.** The Servicer is expressly not obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to any Successor Servicer or third party. There is no licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates or its contractors, and no mechanism to add them, so a Successor Servicer would have no right to run the platform needed to service the Receivables. This fails both the preferred and fallback positions and is our principal open point.
2. **Absence of any insurance covenant where the counterparty processes personal data.** The Servicer/Custodian holds Obligor personally identifiable information and may contract with other Persons under Section 6.4, with no coverage requirement anywhere in the Agreement. This engages the playbook's walk-away scenario for a vendor processing personal data; the Section 6.3 indemnity does not cure it.
